source_text:
Τὸ δὲ τελειῶσαι τὸ ἔργον τοῦ πατρὸς ἐπὶ τὴν ὅλην οἰκονομίαν ἀναφέρεται, ἧς μέρος καὶ ἡ πρὸς τὴν Σαμαρεῖτιν ὁμιλία καὶ ἡ τῶν ἐκ τῆς πόλεως πιστευσάντων κλῆσις.

μέχρι γὰρ τοῦ· Τετέλεσται· ἐπὶ τοῦ σταυροῦ φθάνει τὸ τελειῶσαι τὸ ἔργον.
pass_a_gloss: And the finishing of the work of the Father is referred upon the whole economy, of which a part is also the converse toward the Samaritan woman and the calling of those from the city who believed. For as far as the “It has been finished” upon the cross the finishing of the work arrives.
pass_b_english: Finishing the Father’s work points to the whole economy — of which this talk with the Samaritan woman and the calling of those from the city who believed are a part.
That finishing reaches as far as [[“It is finished” >> Bible:John 19:30]] on the cross.
